WHY RECOGNITION IS A FELT RE-COGNITION

The mechanism of recognition in the IPVV — the σ-flip, the three registers, and why the change must be felt

  • 026-08-11. The thesis is that recognition is a felt re-cognition. Why "felt"? Why "re-"cognition?
  • is essay answers both by expounding the mechanism the IPVV actually gives. Recognition is a
  • -cognition because it is the return of a self that was never absent ("I was never not"); it is felt
  • cause the change it makes — the σ-flip, the re-positioning of the self from a thing among things to
  • e primary thing — is experienced as a savouring, a camatkāra. This essay reconstructs the mechanism
  • actly: what changes, what does not, and why the change must be felt. It is the mechanism-essay, the
  • ow it actually works" of the recognition-thesis.*

1. The two questions

  • e thesis makes two claims that need explaining:
  • Re-cognition. Why "re-"? If the self was never absent, what is recognized again?
  • Felt. Why felt? If recognition changes positioning, not content, why is the change experienced
  • a savouring?
  • e IPVV answers both, and the answers turn out to be the same mechanism — the σ-flip — seen from two
  • des. This essay expounds that mechanism in full.

2. The mechanism: the σ-flip (the IPVV's "content unchanged, positioning changed")

  • e IPVV states the core of recognition at three registers, all one move: *content unchanged,
  • sitioning changed*. Formalized (from the formal-framework essay), recognition is the operation R that
  • anges the self-positioning parameter σ, with the field-content ⟨Sᵢ, Wᵢ, Γᵢ⟩ identical:
  • `
  • : ⟨Sᵢ, Wᵢ, Γᵢ ; σ₀⟩ → ⟨Sᵢ, Wᵢ, Γᵢ ; σ₁⟩
  • `
  • ere:
  • σ₀ = the self as a thing among things — "an instrument lost among the things of the body and the
  • rld" (V1E). The self mis-taken as an object in the field.
  • σ₁ = the self as the primary, foregrounded — "the primary thing we see" (V1E). The self as the
  • bject, the light in which the field appears.
  • What changes:** σ — the self-positioning.
  • What does not change:** the tuple ⟨Sᵢ, Wᵢ, Γᵢ⟩ — the field content.
  • is is the whole mechanism. Recognition is not the addition of a new object, a new belief, or a new
  • ntent; it is the re-positioning of the self within the same field.

3. Why it is a re-cognition ("I was never not," V1D)

  • cognition is a re-cognition because the self was never absent. The IPVV's second register (V1D):
"The manifestation of the self is not unprecedented. It does not begin to shine at some moment; it
was always shining. The self is un-cut by all three times: past, present, and future. It did not come
into being, and it will not pass away."
  • The argument.** If the self never was absent, then there is nothing for recognition to add — nothing
  • uld be added to an eternal self. The "unprecedented manifestation," the appearance of something new,
  • only apparent; it rests on the eternal, always-manifested knower. So recognition cannot be an
  • tainment; it must be a return — a re-cognition of what was always there.
  • The precise mechanism.** The σ-flip is a re-cognition because the content (the field) was always
  • ere; only the positioning of the self within it changes. The "re-" marks the identity of the content:
  • is the same field, the same self, re-positioned. Recognition re-cognizes — knows again — what was
  • ways present but mis-positioned.

4. Why it is felt (the camatkāra, the σ-flip as savouring)

  • cognition is felt because the σ-flip — the change from σ₀ to σ₁ — is experienced as a savouring.
  • e IPVV's third register (V3P, the lover-union):
"The lover stands near, sought by the slender woman; but as long as he is not recognized, he cannot
be enjoyed. So the world-Lord, always present, always near, is not experienced in his own splendor
until the recognition arises… The single act of recognition turns the un-known nearness into the joy
of union."
  • The argument.** The lover is near — the content is present, never absent. What changes with
  • cognition is the relation: from un-known nearness to the joy of union. And this change is felt —
  • is the joy, the savouring, the camatkāra. The recognition does not bring the lover; it turns the
  • ar into the enjoyed.
  • Why the change must be felt.** The σ-flip is a change in the self's relation to its field — from the
  • lf as a thing (σ₀) to the self as the subject (σ₁). And a change in the self's relation to its world
  • s* experienced — it is felt as the shift from the near-but-un-recognized (the "un-known nearness") to
  • e near-and-enjoyed (the "joy of union"). The felt is not a side-effect of recognition; it is the
  • gister of the σ-flip. Recognition is felt because the re-positioning of the self is a felt event.

5. The mechanism, complete (the three registers as one)

  • e three registers of the IPVV are the same mechanism at three levels:
  • Register | The σ-flip as... | What changes | What does not |
  • ---------|------------------|--------------|---------------|
  • Foregrounding (V1E) | a spatial shift | the self from background-instrument to foreground-primary | the field content |
  • "I was never not" (V1D) | a temporal-eternal grounding | the self from present-but-un-positioned to present-and-recognized | the field content (and the self, never absent) |
  • The lover-union (V3P) | a relational-aesthetic shift | the self from near-but-un-recognized to near-and-enjoyed | the field content (the lover, always near) |
  • All three are: content unchanged, positioning changed.** The foregrounding shows it spatially; the
  • was never not" grounds it in eternity; the lover-union shows it as felt. This is the mechanism of
  • cognition, stated by the IPVV at three registers, and unified by the σ-flip.

6. The felt and the σ-flip: is the joy content?

  • e deepest question about the mechanism is whether the felt — the joy of union — is content. If it
  • , then recognition adds content (the joy), contradicting "nothing added." If it is not, then what is
  • e felt re-cognition?
  • The IPVV's resolution (and the audit's precision).* The felt is not an *additional content; it is
  • e same content, differently valenced — the same field, the same self, experienced under the σ₁
  • sitioning. The joy of union is not a new object added to the field; it is the field experienced when
  • e self stands as the subject rather than as a thing among things. The σ-flip changes the valence of
  • e field, not its content.
  • is is why the tear-apart audit's correction is essential: **recognition removes the identification
  • th the finite self-positioning, not the self-positioning itself.** The felt joy is the field
  • perienced without the identification of the self as a thing; it is not an addition but a
  • -valuation. The felt re-cognition is the σ-flip, and the σ-flip is a change of valence, not of
  • ntent.

7. Why this is the "how it works"

  • e mechanism essay answers the "how":
  • Recognition works because the essence of consciousness is the felt self-grasp (Step 1 of the
  • timate proof) — there is something to recognize.
  • It works as a re-cognition because the self was never absent (V1D) — there is nothing to add,
  • ly to re-position.
  • It works as a σ-flip because the change is one of positioning, not content (V1E/V1D/V3P) — the
  • me field, the self re-positioned.
  • It is felt because the re-positioning of the self is a change in the self's relation to its
  • eld, and that change is experienced as the camatkāra, the joy of union (V3P).
  • e mechanism is one operation — the σ-flip — with a felt register. Recognition is the felt
  • -cognition of the self because it is the σ-flip of the felt self-grasp: the change of the self's
  • sitioning within its field, experienced as a savouring. That is the complete mechanism, and it is
  • y the thesis is true: recognition works, it is a re-cognition, and it is felt.

8. The boundary

  • e mechanism is [T] in the IPVV and complete for the finite field. What it does not establish is
  • e universalization — the step from "the field's self re-positions" to "all fields are one self." The
  • flip operates on the field's self-grasp; whether all such self-grasps are one is the commitment
  • tep 5 of the ultimate proof). The mechanism explains how recognition works for the finite field; it
  • es not force the identity of all fields. That is the boundary, and it is the same in every document
  • the library.
